utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Although I would hope that production of exhibits can be left to the end of the evidence, it may be helpful if I make a mental note or spoken note as we go along of those that are potential candidates for production, and thus far it would seem to me that the video of the 1991 demonstrations and the police response, the video of the Badza funeral, and this map, the marked mapped taken from the Kula wall are the three candidates to date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Nice: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, I want to deal this morning, in order to ensure that I cover in the time I allow myself essential topics, a few Croatian issues. We'll then move through Bosnia and return to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness have this --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are not having the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you hear it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday at the beginning of his cross-examination, Mr. Nice invoked or referred to some document from a meeting of the Council for the Harmonisation of State Positions, attended by Mr. Cosic and others, and I asked for this document to be supplied to me. You indeed made that order, but I still haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'd be very disappointed if that hasn't been done; in fact, more than disappointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, I very much hope not. We -- believe me, we are flooded with material in this case and with this witness, and if by oversight I failed to remember to check that that particular document, which is an existing exhibit, had been provided, it's a matter for which I take complete responsibility. It will be done, and cross-examination -- re-examination will not start, in any event, until tomorrow because I shall be all today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, please ensure that it is passed to the accused at the earliest opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. It's the -- what it is is the minute, so that the accused can remember, it's the minute of one of the Council of Harmonisation meetings which we hadn't been provided with the full transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Dicklich, who is very reliable, will see to that, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, can you have a look, please, at this document coming your way. It's an existing exhibit, 607, tab 13, English on the overhead projector. It's a document of the 1st of October of 1991. It is described as secret. It goes from Colonel Stevan Mitrevski and goes to the federal Secretariat for National Defence and Administration. If you turn over, please, to the third paragraph from the end of this document, which is an existing exhibit which deals with action in Croatia, and if you, Mr. Prendergast, take us to the second page and the bottom of it. "There is a rumour among the JNA members located in that area, that Arkan goes into action only after the JNA units mop up the area and then he ... and that area and commits crimes. They think that Arkan is doing it with a full support of the SDB of Serbia." So this was a complaint in October 1991 that Arkan was committing crimes with SDB of Serbia's support. Was Arkan acting with impunity from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge whatsoever about what is contained in this paragraph. I will remind you that in 1990 and 1991 I was in Kosovo dealing with the problems of Kosovo. I see this information for the first time, and I am hearing for the first time about the substance of this passage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1991, throughout those periods, you were in Kosovo, were you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part of 1990 and 1991, I was in Kosovo. I cannot tell you exactly how much time during that period, but certainly more than six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before Arkan was assassinated he was well rumoured to be a criminal in many ways, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, such information about him existed, but not in my possession. I did not have such information ex officio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is just to remind the Judges and for speed, a still from yesterday's video of Badza's funeral in 1997, and we can see that behind the accused and between him and Lilic, who is on our right, the accused's left, there's Arkan. Until his assassination, no attempt was made by your police force to investigate his crimes, to arrest him, to control him in any way. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what crimes you are referring to. I believe that the police of Serbia did not have specific knowledge about any particular crime of that unit. And anyway, according to all I know, he was part of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and I personally learned all I know about it at the end of 1995 when I spent some time in Vukovar and the surrounding area with my units. Before that period, I was totally unaware of Arkan and his activity except what I could read from the newspaper and hear on the TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is Arkan in the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You can see Lilic -- you can see Lilic behind the accused and to his left and our right, the man with the moustache that he wore at that time, and then immediately between the two of them, the head is the head the Arkan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stevanovic, we can't see you here because -- but you're presumably one of these heads with a military or, rather, a police hat on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness. No microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness. Would you repeat that, General. The microphone wasn't on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As you saw yesterday, I read a eulogy at this commemorative meeting. I was part of this procession, and I remember Arkan was indeed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can see that Arkan was allowed to stand as close as he does to the accused and to Lilic.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he wasn't close. Maybe this is an optical trick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is somewhere deep down, and we cannot really see who is next to Lilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The Djeletovci oil fields lie to the south of Vukovar and thus the east of Croatia. Yes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand this place name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I'm not familiar with that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you not? Is it not the case that in the early part of the 1990s money from the Djeletovci oil fields was used by those engaged in both war and crime to make profits for themselves and even to fund fighting? Do you not remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or is the position that you realise already where I'm aiming, Mr. Stevanovic, and you don't want to remember?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely know nothing about it. The place is totally unfamiliar to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We discussed lightly the Skorpions the other day. Is it the case that one of their early functions, the Skorpions, was to guard the Djeletovci oil fields, thus indeed to enable those who were profiting from them to profit from them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Skorpions are concerned, I have told all I know, and that is that they existed as a group. I don't know as part of what, which forces, but I know nothing about the link between Djeletovci and the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at another existing exhibit very briefly, 466, tab 12. A copy for the accused. This is a document dated the 8th of January, 1992, coming from the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Two different dates, one in hand and one in type. It comes from Badza, Radovan Stojicic, and it certifies that somebody called Miljkovic has been a volunteer in the units of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem since December 1991. So your boss, Badza, working in Croatia. How come?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I knew that Stojicic, as an individual, spent some time in Baranja and Eastern Srem -- or, rather, Eastern Srem while I was in Kosovo. At that time, he was not my superior. As to the grounds for his stay there and the modality, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he was a volunteer or in some way cooperating with the authorities of Serbian Krajina, I don't know. I never saw this document before and all I can say is that this is not his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was an assistant minister or the assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure. At that time, I don't think he was assistant minister. I think he became assistant minister when he returned from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which case what was his job before he left?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, he was an employee in the police administration at the time, but I really can't remember the name of his exact position. I think he was involved in some independent work in the then police administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... unless it's to try and defend the obvious position that he was working for the DB and was working in Croatia at the time of the war? Why do you say he was a volunteer? Where do you get that from?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I do not wish to defend anything or anybody. I'm just telling what I know, and I'm sorry if I'm being repetitive. But for those two years, I was involved in completely different work and I was not in Belgrade at all. I was in Pristina. I had a specific job to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that I'm telling you is only what I learnt from the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at another document which would be a new exhibit, if produced. While that's coming on, isn't it right that Badza was actually the head of the special anti-terrorist unit of the Serbian MUP in 1991? Think back.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a commander of a special anti-terrorist unit, but again, I think that he went to Baranja or Slavonia after he was replaced as commander by Zivko Travkovic. All I'm saying is that it is a strong likelihood. I cannot be absolutely sure, but I think it is almost certainly the way I'm telling it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, dated the 30th of June 1994, in a format of intelligence explained to us by General Vasiljevic, I think, purports to come from Djuro Celic, a major, and has been delivered to various destinations. If we look at the content of this document, there's only one place I really want you to turn to at the moment. In the English version it's page 2 of 4. In the original, Mr. Stevanovic, you'll find it on the second page, about a third of the way down, and we see these entries: "The VRSK and the army of Yugoslavia, the VJ, representatives held three meetings with ... Fikret Abdic in Velika Kladusa, with the aim of preparing an offensive attack by the AP ZB forces to regain seized territory and liberate new territories ending at the Cazin area." At these meetings, Abdic accepted a proposal of a decision on the offensive activities which were to start at 3.00 and stated that on the 21st of June he had a meeting with the President of Serbia attended by Mikulic, Celeketic, Mladic, and Peric and Stanisic, Abdic stating that Milosevic ordered Abdic had to win. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Were you aware of Abdic's communications with and support from this accused?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know nothing about this. You're asking me mostly questions which I cannot answer. I'm seeing this document for the first time and I'm hearing for the first time about this meeting and everything you just quoted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the format of the document?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that and we'll look at the next document, please. For Croatia I only have a few more to go. This, similarly, would be a new exhibit. It was seized in June of 2004 from the state archives in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, was that last item an existing exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. It would have been a new exhibit but in light of the answers, I shan't press it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document is a communication of the 22nd of July of 1994 from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and it's an operations report, as we can see on the first page, Mr. Prendergast, on the situation in the autonomous province of Western Bosnia. I'm only interested in the last page now and the second page for you, Mr. Stevanovic. Such reports, we see, were sent to the president of the Republic of Serbia and others, and the Republic of Serbia MUP, Jovica Stanisic. Is it right that reports on progress in the autonomous province of Western Bosnia were circulated to the MUP and indeed to this accused?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I'm hearing about this. I've never seen this document before, and of course I can see that it was submitted to the MUP of Serbia, Jovica Stanisic, which means the state security sector. But let me remind you that I was in the Republic of Serbian Krajina from late 1995 until August 1996. That is the period about which I know something. About the period that you're asking me, I know absolutely nothing except for what I could learn from the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were in charge of special units as from the early 1990s, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in charge of special units. I was in charge of what was referred to in our language as Special Purpose Units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were very much a trusted senior policeman, or at least a trusted policeman. You rose to the rank of chief inspector. Can you not help us, really, Mr. Stevanovic, with whether relations between what was going on in Western Bosnia and Belgrade were as described in this document, or is the position that you will not help us?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely not the case that I do not wish to assist you, it's just that my opinion about these documents can only be superficial because I was in no way involved until 1990, although I was an inspector, that much is true. But I had a strictly defined purview and competencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next document -- I withdraw that one, then, if that's the witness's answer. I'm not going to trouble us further with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the next one, which also would be a new document. This is a document dated the 31st of July, 1995, so we're now within your period of time in Eastern Slavonia, I think, or Eastern Croatia, in any event. And it says this: "On the 30th of July of 1995, at 14.50 hours at the line of defence of the 101st Detachment ..." and then it says this: 1, somebody from the SUP Secretariat of the Interior, 2 and 3 similarly identified, and then 4, Vujica Petrovic, Belgrade SUP from Stari Grad, Vladimir Garic, Belgrade SUP also from Stari Grad, the old city. And this information is being sent to the Republic of Serbia MUP police administration in Belgrade. This document shows, doesn't it, that Serbian SUP or MUP employees were fighting in Croatia. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document, for a change, that I can tell you something about. It is true that these are members of the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, and in this connection it is important to tell you that this 101st Detachment indeed existed. These members were policemen of the MUP of Serbia who, to put it approximately, expressed their desire to -- to go to the Republic of Serbian Krajina because they were natives of that area. Before that time, they were employees of the MUP of Serbia. And the decision was made to let them go voluntarily to the Republic of Serbian Krajina, whereas the role of the ministry was to give them permission and approval to do that. And once there, they would be resubordinated to the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. So these people went voluntarily to the RSK, and this is a completely different story than what we see in other documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you remember these two applied to go because they came from the area, or are you saying that this is some general policy of which these two may be members?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any of these four individually. I don't know any of them personally. But I do know the circumstances and the manner in which this detachment went to Knin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where will we find the documents of their subordination or resubordination to the other army?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in the archives of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. This document, as you can see, is a document from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. Otherwise, this ministry would not have informed the MUP of Serbia that these people had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Saying that these people are volunteers and raising as a possibility that Badza was a volunteer without any evidence is necessary to dissociate Serbia from this fighting, isn't it, Mr. Stevanovic, and that's why you're saying these things.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not the reason. I have given you a lengthy explanation. When on the territory of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina, I told you when units of the Ministry of the Interior went there. I said quite clearly that they went pursuant to the decision of the appropriate organs of the ministry. In this case, the situation is different. These are all people who are born in those areas and who expressed a wish to go there in this period, and they asked the Ministry of the Interior to give them permission to do this, to go there and to join the MUP of Republika Srpska Krajina, and therein lies the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, how many police officers would have gone as volunteers to the RSK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't recall precisely, but between 2 and 400, several hundred as part of this unit mentioned here. In the ministry of Serbia, they were simply organised, given permission, they took their equipment and weapons with them, and in this way their wish was granted to help the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska Krajina where all of them to a man originated. Not a single member of this unit had been born outside the Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: While there, who paid them? Who was responsible for their conditions of service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They continued as employees of the Ministry of the Interior. One might say they were on paid leave as for their status in the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does what you've just said also apply to Badza?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume it applies to Badza, but I'm not aware of the facts pertaining to Badza. I believe the situation was similar, but of course he was not born in those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you're saying there was no policy to assign them there. They were not assigned there by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it was initiated by a large number of those men who felt that they had to go and help. The Ministry of the Interior accepted their request, they granted it, and they made it possible for them to go there, as I have explained. But I was never there myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they were on unpaid leave, what's the purpose of writing to inform the Serbian MUP of their being injured? Why bother?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is quite normal for the MUP of Serbia to be informed that their employees had been wounded. This is not a combat report. It's not a report on the result of combat, if they took part in combat at all. So there is no report being submitted to the MUP of Serbia about what they were doing there. They were simply being informed that four men who were their employees had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've had evidence via Exhibit 549, tab 26, and a witness that following the Erdut agreement 300 policemen from the Serbian MUP in Srem and Baranja were to be left as long as possible in the territory of Croatia and that you were in charge of that unit. Is that right? And just to help you, the witness -- the witness --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. That's right. There's no need for you to assist me. Of course, the need to remain there as long as possible was something that the local police organs in Republika Srpska Krajina requested. It was not initiated from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, another -- one more document coming the witness's way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell us, please, who is Branislav Vakic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Branislav Vakic. He was a deputy in the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia. He comes from Nis, and as far as I know, he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was a leader of or partaker in the paramilitary group of that party; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met that man in Bajina Basta, and he told me that he belonged to a unit of the army of Republika Srpska in the area of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You fought alongside him?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't fight alongside him. Due to circumstances, my unit and his unit were in the same area -- or, rather, my unit was in the same area where his unit allegedly was, but I have no information about his unit or its members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then just this for your comment: If you look at the English version, first page, foot of the page, please, and in the newspaper article that you've got, and it's a little hard to read -- I'll just see if I can find the reference. Thank you. Second page, please, Mr. Stevanovic, for you, and you'll see -- it's not very clear. It's at the foot of the page, but I'm just going to read what Vakic is reported to have said when asked about cooperation with the MUP of Serbia, he having dealt at great length with the army. He says this: "There is much such cooperation in battles from Skelani to Srebrenica. We fought alongside the special forces of the MUP under the command of Obrad Stevanovic, the third man in the Serbian MUP. I had excellent cooperation with him on the Skelani battlefield. He had his headquarters in Bajina Basta, and I would travel from Skelani to talk to him. I would go to him whenever I needed something, and he would issue orders about where one should go. From the beginning of April until 25 May last year, we fought alongside the special forces of the MUP." Over the page, please. "A little later, the MUP of Serbia invited us to prepare ourselves and, if need be, fight together with them. We responded to the invitation, I gathered the men, and we went to a training centre at the Tara Mountain during July ... At that time, I was in contact with 'Frenki' of the MUP special forces. At the moment I gathered a sufficient number of volunteers he would send an official MUP bus from Belgrade to Nis. From Nis, my volunteers left for Tara to undergo training. At that time, I had about 400 people from Nis, Zajecar, Pirot, and Kragujevac. From there, Chetniks and volunteers, together with MUP special forces, were supposed to set off towards Srebrenica or Gorazde if the Turkish converts launched a major offensive." Vakic said that in an interview when he was, I think, already a member of the legislature or something to that effect. I'll get his position. Is what he says correct? He was an Assembly deputy.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it in a nutshell, these are semi-truths. Some facts are correct and some are totally incorrect. Everything you have quoted requires a detailed explanation if, of course, you allow me. Secondly, I can endeavour to recall the context. I read this article a long time ago, I can say that, and it was written after a political conflict that took place at the time between the Serb Radical Party and the Socialist Party of Yugoslavia. The text is full of emotion in this respect because the position of the Serb Radical Party is contrasted and opposed to the standpoint of the Socialist Party. So it contains many inaccuracies. To explain, it's true I met that person two or three times in my headquarters in Bajina Basta. I never invited him over. I received him Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. because he asked to be received. He told me that there were positions between Srebrenica and Skelani where he had his unit as part of the army of Republika Srpska. He did not ask me for any kind of cooperation. He did not ask me to participate in any kind of joint operation, and as far as the police is concerned, there were no combat operations there at all. Only one policeman was killed while searching the terrain. The entire operation lasted ten days. After ten days, the last policeman from Serbia withdrew over the River Drina to the Republic of Serbia because there was no need for us to remain there. His unit, and I don't know what their strength was or anything else, they remained part of the army of Republika Srpska. Had they been under our command in any way, they would have been sent there under our command and withdrawn under our command. But they were already there when we arrived and they remained there after we had withdrawn. Everything else, as for training and issuing of orders and so on and so forth, none of this is correct. Not a single man of his was ever part of a unit of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You read the article. Did you ever sue over it? You an important man, he a public figure, did you ever litigate over this article?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I didn't sue him, although I had reason to. I also had reason to sue the person we discussed in private session, but I didn't do that. I am a professional, a high-ranking policeman. It would be silly of me to sue everyone who says something incorrect about me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were indeed number three in the MUP, as he suggests. That's how important you were; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely incorrect that I was the number three man in the MUP at the time. There were at least ten men above me at that time. At that time, I was the commander of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question on Croatia, probably altogether or certainly for the moment, are these: We looked at this map yesterday taken from the ceremony, from the wall of the Kula premises. We looked at the names associated with various locations for which there are markers on the map, and you've now had an overnight to think about it. Do you have any reason to doubt that the MUP of Serbia engaged in all the areas marked in Croatia on that map; and, if so, you tell us which ones you say are wrong.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you where the MUP was active. And all these places are not even marked here, so there are places missing here where members of the PJP were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you would so good, because time is short. My question is: The ones marked and identified by Frenki, are they correct, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all my knowledge, I can't answer this because I don't know where Frenki was or where his units were later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you can't help us and we'll move on to something else. Can I have the map back, please. Before we turn, as we inevitably must, to Bosnia, I just want to look to one other thing for a general proposition. In 1996, the accused's local elections were challenged, it being suggested that the accused had rigged the elections, and eventually he succumbed but not until after many demonstrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we just play this video, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is an interpretation into another language here that bothers me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not concerned with this passage of it particularly. The problem with Sanction is we can't select passages as easily as with other devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all I wanted you to look at. That's your police dealing with demonstrators who were complaining about rigged elections. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. Yesterday I said something about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's an indication of the measure of violence that your police were prepared to deliver. Now, I ask you that question for this reason: You have been a very trusted man, Mr. Stevanovic, I'm going to suggest to you, for the following reasons: You were trusted with the takeover of the MUP building in Belgrade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was not trusted with it, I was assigned the task. It probably means the same, but you're using this word purposely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were trusted with being in charge of the police at a time that was important for the accused's attempted retention of power in 1996, 1997.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was entrusted with this task at a time when it was assessed that I was the best man to carry it out. Before you put a question to me, if possible, you always have three or four incorrect statements, but you don't give me a chance to respond to them. When you make a statement, allow me to give you my opinion about it. Otherwise, I cannot say everything I want to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is fair enough on the witness's part. We have been listening to a lot of comment this morning and not questioning, and the witness is right to come to his own defence on that matter so that the Court receives proper evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And the Chamber will, too, when it is appropriate. Mr. Nice, you are to desist from the introductory comments before you put your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I have been, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, is the interview of Vakic one of the candidate --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It is a candidate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We haven't been offered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. You're quite right to remind me, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question to which your last answer was given and Mr. Kay's objection was made read: "You were trusted with being in charge of the police at a time that was important for the accused's attempted retention of power." Did you understand that question?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did understand it, but that's not the way I think. I accepted the duty when it was entrusted to me. The person who entrusted me with the task probably knew why he was doing that and why he had selected me to carry it out. I did not make any connection between this and the president of Serbia, the Prime Minister, or the speaker of the Assembly. I was not on friendly relations with any of them privately. I did not have any personal links with then. I'd just been a policeman in uniform for a long time, for 15 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let's go back from 1996 to 1995. You told us, I think me, yesterday or the day before in questioning, about how you escorted DutchBat out of Srebrenica. Just tell us again where it was you went.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct that I escorted DutchBat out of Srebrenica. I took over DutchBat on the bridge between Bratunac and Ljubovija. I met the battalion commander in a hotel in Bratunac. I only came as far as Bratunac, which is perhaps a kilometre across the Drina from the place in Serbia called Ljubovija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who instructed you to take the part that you took in seeing DutchBat out of former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order to undertake measures to secure the battalion on their passage through Serbia was given to me by the deputy minister, Mr. Stojicic, who was then the head of the sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date upon which you were seeing DutchBat out was what date?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that. I think it was July or August. I know it was very hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give us a date the last time I asked you about this?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- very well. I'll come back to that, I think. You told us already in answer to the accused that you had a job supervising some part of the border between Bosnia-Herzegovina or RS, as you might call it, and Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long had you had the job of supervising that border?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The job of supervising the border and the in-depth securing of the border is the daily task of the border police units. This is an ongoing task. However, measures at the border were stepped up as of 1991 and quite certainly as of 1992. And these measures entailed strengthening of the numbers of police in the border area and their intensified activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you there? What period of time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was the Chief of Staff in Bajina Basta for several months, perhaps three months, more or less. After this, the headquarters moved to Prijepolje and other people were in charge of the staff there. This was in 1993, from perhaps February or March, April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in 1995?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The presence of police units from Serbia, as I have already explained, in the sector between Visegrad and Bajina Basta, between Rudo and Priboj, lasted until 1996 when 800 combatants of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were received after the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you there in 1995 dealing with that border?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, including when I went to Visegrad and the positions that I mentioned in responding to your previous questions. I would come there from time to time, spend a brief period of time, until the unit withdrew from that area, that is to say up until 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if we look at the period of the Srebrenica attack, and you understand, Mr. Stevanovic, that that's what I'm interested in, were you the officer with responsibility or some responsibility for that border?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Ministry of the Interior, there is the department for the border police, and it is the department which deals with the border crossing controls and everything else that happens in the border belt. My units or, rather, the general units or the PJP units during that period of time, as I've explained it, were just reinforcing security at the border and the boarder belt, including what the police did in the area behind the border, and we spent quite some time in discussing that previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the months that you were there doing this included the months of the Srebrenica massacre.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They include the whole of 1995, that is to say including the events in Srebrenica. But the events themselves are something that I absolutely did not know about at that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The DutchBat came out before, during, or after the massacre? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether the massacre occurred, when it occurred. I can just believe it or disbelieve it, but I have no actual knowledge of it. I don't know whether it happened and whether it happened before or after the DutchBat withdrew. I simply don't know. And with respect to that battalion, I had a very specific task and assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the border that you supervised, or that you and other troops supervised, went down to Priboj; yes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up to Priboj or, rather, the border with Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Priboj is sort of to the east of Gorazde, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think so, at least, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just north of Priboj there's a little crossing called Raca.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a Raca, but I'm not sure whether it's a crossing. I don't recall whether it is in fact an official border crossing. There is an official border crossing at Uvac and Kotroman. Possibly between the two there is a crossing which is used from time to time, a provisional one, but quite certainly it's not a permanent border crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when somebody or some unit has to pass from or had to pass from Serbia into the RS or Bosnia-Herzegovina, depending on how we describe it, whose leave would they need, whose permission?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean other units, other people's units, or what? I'm not sure what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us, you were supervising the crossing. Was it basically a closed crossing and people had to have permission to pass? Was it a dangerous crossing that they needed to be escorted to pass? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of my answers to a previous question, I said this clearly: Control and supervision of border crossings at official border crossings was something that was done by the sector within the Ministry of the Interior. It is the sector for the border police. So these stepped-up measures do not relate to the official border crossings. And I've just remembered, because I was thinking about another area, the Raca border crossing does indeed exist as an official border crossing but it is quite Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. a lot further to the north, the north of Sabac, in fact, and it has nothing to do with the area that we were discussing, and we were discussing the southern reaches of the border with Republika Srpska. Raca is to the extreme north of the border with Republika Srpska on the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there are two Racas possibly, but there is certainly one in the position I asked you about and which you remembered to the east of Gorazde, and we'll just have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember a place like that. Possibly it is there, but I just can't remember anything with that name there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I did ask you a question about it. I asked you if it was east of Gorazde and you said it was. Are you now wanting to change your recollection, or --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I stayed that Priboj was east of Gorazde. Perhaps we misunderstood each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did. Just have a look at this map so we can orientate the Court to what I'm talking about. Certain points have been highlighted. Just to orientate the Judges and everybody else, Srebrenica to the north with Bratunac very nearby but we haven't marked it yet, Bajina Basta to the right, Gorazde there, and then you'll see marked on the east at a border Raca. Do you see it? No. There it is.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that lies north of Priboj, which we can see below that, this was in the area of your control. Now, tell me, please, if a force of soldiers wished to pass from Serbia into Bosnia-Herzegovina, would it need somebody's permission? This is in the middle of 1995.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crossing of the border between the Republic of Serbia and Republika Srpska at that time, when we're talking about citizens from Bosnia-Herzegovina, for example, and also citizens from Serbia, that came under the ID card regime. That is to say they needed ID cards and not travelling documents, other types of travelling documents. Now, when we're talking about this particular place, the name of which is Raca, it is quite illogical that there should be a border crossing there because there's a border crossing anyway at a place called Uvac, and you can see right there, very close by, is Uvac, and that's the official border crossing between the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Srpska Krajina. So it's quite illogical that this place Raca should be used for that. It's a very small place and I'm hearing it for the first time and I can see that it exists on the map and this is the first time that I realise that, that there's a place by that name so close to Priboj. But Uvac is the official border crossing, and I'm indicating this quite clearly. It is south-west of this place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A couple of points I'd like you to dwell on. If I could have the map back, please. You're aware, aren't you, that the RS has conceded within the last year that there was at Srebrenica a massacre of some 7.000 people. You must be aware of that.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been following that from the information media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you gave an answer that you didn't know whether the massacre happened. Is that seriously your position, that you don't know if the massacre happened despite the concession that was been made by the RS?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not know at the time, at the time when I provided security for the DutchBat through Serbia. At that point in time, I had no knowledge or intimations of that event. And of course that, of late, I have gained information about that from the information media, but no official information. And of course I do believe it. I have no reason to doubt that something happened there. Of course I can't speak about the details. I read about it in the papers just like any other citizen of Serbia is able to read about it in the papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: DutchBat left after the massacre, or most of it, had happened, on the 21st of July. You were asked to accompany them, as you say, from Bratunac, and I'm going to ask you this: Were you the man asked to escort them because you could be trusted in circumstances where everybody knew that a massacre had happened? Is that why you were chosen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't know that. Absolutely not. The assignment was a serious assignment because an entire battalion had to pass through the Republic of Serbia and the demand for escort came from them. I don't know through whom, but it wasn't the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia who took the initiative for us to escort them. We met the request of the Dutch Battalion who asked to be provided for security in passing through the Republic of Serbia. The only unusual thing was that there was great insistence on the fact that full escort should be provided through the Republic of Serbia up until the Croatian border, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long did that crossing take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The crossing through Serbia took as long as it was necessary to travel those kilometres, perhaps 2 hours, perhaps a little more. From Ljubovija to Batrovac near Sid, and that distance is about 100 to 150 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, I'm going to suggest to you that, amongst other things that may have come to your knowledge, is this: That earlier in July a detachment of Skorpions had passed into Bosnia-Herzegovina through a border known as Raca. Think back. Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that very clearly, Mr. Prosecutor. There is absolutely no question of any other formation, other unit during this involvement of the PJP across the border was in their composition. I claim that with absolute certainty, and I've said on a number of occasions that I personally controlled the work of those units in the Drina area and the area of Visegrad, Rudo, Priboj, and Bajina Basta. Not a single solitary unit or group ever belonged to that composition. This is the first time that I hear that the Skorpions were in Serbia at all. And if they were moving towards Srebrenica, as you say, then it is highly unlikely that they would have crossed at Priboj, because then they would have crossed at Bajina Basta because Srebrenica is just across the Drina River vis-a-vis Bajina Basta. And it is three or four times longer crossing at Priboj. And if they were under the control of any unit from Serbia, they wouldn't have chosen this particular place, Raca, south of the main Raca. And you can look at that on the map and see for yourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look, before we move on to what that unit did, to a few other documents on which I'd like your assistance, please. This is a document from the Republika Srpska dated the 23rd of June of 1995 to the president of the Republika Srpska in Pale, their seat outside Sarajevo. "Pursuant to your communication ... We hereby wish to advise you that by 1000 hours on 23 June 1995 our Collection Centres in Janja and Zvornik have handed over to the VRS/Republika Srpska army/armed forces a total of 1586 conscripts delivered by the MUP Serbia, and of this, 149 conscripts were handed over to the MUP staff on Jahorina." Signed by Deputy Minister Kovac. Do you remember first in this line of questions the process whereby conscripts, as they were described, for the RS found in Serbia were rounded up and handed back?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me say that this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice is asking the wrong question, or perhaps the interpretation is wrong. He said conscripts from Serbia. We're not dealing with conscripts from Serbia here but conscripts from Republika Srpska. That's quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Conscripts from Republika Srpska rounded up in -- from Republika Srpska, rounded up in Serbia and handed back. Do you remember that happening?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me say first of all that this is the first time I see this document. Of course I know what it refers to, and it refers to this: Rounding up conscripts of Republika Srpska who happened to be on the territory of the Republic of Serbia pursuant to requests by the military authorities of Republika Srpska and pursuant to the law on conscripts or defence of the day, I'm not quite sure which law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to this extent, shortly before Srebrenica, over a thousand conscripts delivered up by Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: These will all be candidates for admission in due course, if I can so indicate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but Serbia -- I do apologise, but -- may I be allowed to answer? Serbia didn't hand over these people. It was pursuant to requests from the military authorities of Republika Srpska. They rounded them up pursuant to the law on conscripts and handed them over to Republika Srpska as conscripts of Republika Srpska and not as conscripts of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we can look at the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to read the first paragraph to check the accuracy of translation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Pursuant to your communication, confidential No. 01-1118-39/95 of the 22nd of June, 1995, we hereby wish to advise you that by the 23rd of June, 1995 by 1000 hours from our collection centres in Janja and Zvornik a total of 1586 military conscripts were handed over to the VRS, which was handed over by the MUP of Serbia." That's the first sentence. "Of this number, 149 conscripts were handed over to the MUP staff on Jahorina." Of course from this document we can't see who they were, and the term "isporucio" or "delivered" was wrongly used.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Handed over" or "delivered"; "isporucio" in the B/C/S, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document, please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document, please. Dated the 26th of June of 1995. The document reads -- it comes from Pale, and it reads: "During the day there were no ... operations on the defence line held by police forces." And then down a little bit further, under "Other events," it says: "The Serbian MUP and the Republika Srpska MUP have sent 350 members of Special Purposes Units. On 27 June ... they will be engaged on the Trnovo front." Now, by all means read the rest of the document, of course. Would you like, please, to explain how the Republika Srpska is setting out with the Serbian MUP, together with the Republika Srpska MUP, has sent 350 members of Special Purpose Units to be engaged on the Trnovo front.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm really not clear on what this means. At that time from the MUP of the Republika Serbia [as interpreted], nobody was in this sector, especially not special units in the MUP of Serbia. There aren't that many for this number to be reinforced. There must be a mistake of some kind here. It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document that was seized in Banja Luka police station in 2004, or is it --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state that during this period of time from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia on the territory of Republika Srpska there were only units as I explained them, the ones I explained were there, in the eastern part of Republika Srpska, in the Visegrad-Priboj sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document, then, please, which is this one.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does this document have a signature or a date or anything like that? I apologise, but could you tell me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... asked the question. I have explained it was seized from the police station in 2004 and it is as it appears.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim and state that during this period of time on the territory of Republika Srpska there was not a single unit except for what I explained about the Visegrad-Rudo area. Now, the second fact that is important here is that the special MUP units in Serbia have existed -- that is to say there is the SAJ, which numbers a maximum of 150 men. So Serbia hasn't got more than 150 men manning the special units. And in Visegrad and Rudo or, rather, the area of Visegrad and Rudo there were these special units there, the PJ units. And, of course, in 1995, in the late autumn, and we're talking about spring quite obviously here, we had the PJP units engaged in the Banja Luka-Prijedor-Doboj sector and so on, whereas this period is quite obviously between those two dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me a minute. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at another document. Now, this document was obtained from the MUP building, I think, in Pale in the summer of 2003, and we see what it is. It's Special Police Brigade, dated the 30th of June, coming from the forward command post at Trnovo, and it says this: "On the 29th of June of 1995, a combat police group, comprised of the 4th SOP, special police detachment, and the 7th special police detachment, and the Kajman police detachment of the Serbia MUP along with the VRS offensive forces launched an attack on Lucevik ... which is under the enemy's control and is of extreme importance for the ... Trnovo-Sarajevo road." Further down the page. In fact, at its foot. We've just about got it there. "During the combats of the 29th of June ... two members of the SBP (one from the 4th and the other from the 7th ...) and two from the Serbia MUP were wounded." Now, you told us, of course, a long time ago now that you knew about everything that was done by the Serbian MUP in Bosnia and Croatia, and I'd like you please to explain what this means.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite unknown to me. I never heard of the name Kajman. That's the first time that I hear of such a name, and I stand by my answer so far. I'm really surprised how come in such documents the MUP of Serbia is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you the answer is that the MUP of Serbia was indeed involved, and what's more, I'm going to suggest, Mr. Stevanovic, you know about that.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Prosecutor. You cannot know better than I know myself what I knew and know. I did not know, and I claim that with full responsibility. If you prove that I did know, you can arrest me straight away. There is not a single piece of anything to show that I know anything about this document, a single indication. And I claim - let me be more precise - from the composition of the public security sector, quite certainly nobody was on the territory of Republika Srpska at all during this period of time except the units that I explained to you in answering the previous question. That is the only truth. And I really don't know how it is possible that somebody wrote this down. Who was suffering under a delusion I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, is it possible that the MUP might have been involved and you would not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theoretically, Mr. President, everything is possible, but during this period of time I truly was in my -- I was deeply convinced that I knew about all the activities of the public security sector. Of course the state security sector was something I didn't deal with, so I assume that this was the state -- had it been the state security sector, it would have said so whereas here it is written the MUP of Serbia, and in principle when you say the MUP of Serbia it means the public sector -- security sector, so I say with certainty the units certainly weren't there. I cannot claim whether some individual might have been there while he was on leave or holiday or a group of that kind, but I assume that even in that case, were that the case, I would have had to have some knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the second page there is the signature of the deputy commander. Are you familiar with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I met this gentleman in Belgrade, that's all, at the faculty. I don't know him personally, nor did I have any meetings with him during this period of time or during the war at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to follow on from His Honour Judge Robinson's question, even though you were in the state as opposed to this -- you were in the public, as you say, as opposed to the state security part of the MUP, given your seniority and in particular given your role in respect of the border between the Republika Srpska and Serbia, you would have had to know of the movement of troops from one to the other, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sectors which were covered by these units from the PJP units, it would be logical for us to know. However, the border crossings, official ones, were controlled by another service, the border service and sector. Normal communication between the two republics went on at official border crossings. So -- and I can't speak about that in detail because that was the job of another service. That was the regime, the border crossing regime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me, please. If there was any intention from your political leaders or from anybody else to move troops of Serbia in some improper way from Serbia into Republika Srpska, your cooperation would be essential, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean if some unit had to pass across the border?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said. Border crossings take place at official border crossings where there is clear-cut and defined procedure under which any citizen in any status can pass in either direction, going to or coming from, and that was the administration of the border police that was in charge of that. So the details about border crossings is something I don't really know about. My units covered an area where in principle you couldn't cross the border. That is to say there was prevention of illegal border crossings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your evidence earlier was that you were reinforcing those border units, and you were doing that not only during the Srebrenica events but from a period before that. Why was it necessary for that reinforcement to take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I explained that, too, but let me repeat. But I think it is important to clarify this point: The border crossing police units controlled official border crossings and administer the procedure for proper border crossing. The police units of general purpose, that is to say municipal units, if we can put it that way, control the border in-depth, where border crossings are prohibited or between two official border crossings. The special units, that is to say the PJP units, strengthen control, first and foremost, between border crossings -- between the official border crossings, not the official border crossings themselves because the special services did that. The reason we did this is logical: There were armed conflicts in Republika Srpska that had arisen, and armed conflicts across a certain line, of course, reflect on the territory of Serbia itself in the following sense: Unlawful border crossings, trafficking across the border, crimes, and so on. And the basic essential reason was to act as a prevention force and prevent the armed conflicts from the territory of Republika Srpska from spreading to the territory of the Republic of Serbia. And this was particularly pertinent after the abductions that took place from the trains and buses that I mentioned earlier on. To prevent storming by paramilitary groups, to prevent communication lines and roads which stretch along the Drina River, along the border belt, to protect the towns who are on the border belt, such as Bajina Basta and so on and so forth, to protect the bridges as well. So there were a number of tasks and assignments. I am trying to recall them all now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will take the adjournment now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next document is a former -- a previous exhibit, 432, tab 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, while we're waiting for that, just to confirm something, while we're waiting for that to be distributed, when you said it was an assistant minister, I think, who instructed you to go and collect the DutchBat, would that be Badza who did that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said deputy minister, and that, of course, was Radovan Stojicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, as you can see, is -- comes from or is headed the Republika Srpska, Ministry of the Interior, Pale, 30th of June of 1995. And it says as to the Muslim factor, if we can look at that, it says something the Trnovo front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Have you got the right document, Mr. Prendergast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the impression that this is not the right document. I don't think I spoke about this, about the Trnovo front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think I've mixed something up, probably. In which case, I'll move on the document that the witness has at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a document dated 30th June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the one we've already looked at, I think, in which case can we --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. This is document 113/95 of the 30th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signature is the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the Kajman group of the Serbian MUP. I think what we're looking at is possibly a slightly different --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we have that one back, please. And while we're locating the document that I had hoped to lay before you, I'll move on to the next one, which is this one. Right. Now, this one is the 1st of July, and it is headed MUP Special Police Brigade, Forward Command Post Trnovo, sent to the MUP, to the deputy minister, to the Vogosca police force, and it says activities commenced the previous day were continued at the Trnovo battlefield on the 30th of June. The combat group included "5th Special Police Detachment, two platoons from Kajman detachment, Plavi blue, and Skorpion (Serbian MUP)". And then if you look further down the page, Mr. Stevanovic, you will find towards the bottom: "In yesterday's clashes, four members of the SBP and three members of the Serbian MUP were lightly wounded." And it's signed by Ljubisa Borovcanin. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my answer would have to be the same as to the previous questions. It would be much better for you to ask the man who signed this. I really have no explanation for this. It would be of assistance if we had a name here. I assert again that the units of the MUP of Serbia were not at that time in that area unless it can be explained by something possible only in theory. The only person who can really explain this is the person who signed. I am really amazed by this. I simply cannot believe that this document exists. What this man understood by the term "MUP of Serbia," I cannot imagine. It is a matter of his own fantasy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fantasy. I see. Very well. Now, this document -- this document dated the 8th of July says -- it comes from Rade Radovic at the Srbinje CJB, public security centre, Srbinje being the newer name, I think, for Foca. It says: "... the following injured policemen of the Serbian MUP were brought from the Treskavica front to the Srbinje hospital: "Milija Vujovic ... Serbian MUP ... "Srdjan Stolic ... Serbian MUP ... "There are no changes from the previous day with regard to the situation ..." How do you explain this document, please?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can explain it only in the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fantasy?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But in this case it is possible to check to whom these people belonged. Of course this does not look like fantasy but I suppose that you have already established to whom these people belonged. I continue to assert that it's not possible that these men belonged to the police units of the MUP of Serbia, and I suppose it is simple to check.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to be asking your assistance, as I said I would, in relation to establishing whether people were from the MUP of Serbia a little later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How could this be checked, Mr. Stevanovic? Mr. Stevanovic, you said it would be simple to check this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assume, Your Honour, that it's possible to ask information from the MUP of Serbia whether these men were ever employed, and we have a unified information system which can tell us where they were employed, when they were born, and all the other personal data. That is no secret. If you allow me, I can make a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. telephone call today and tell you tomorrow who these men are and whether they come from Serbia at all, whether they are employed with the MUP of Serbia or not. I suppose the ministry will grant me that much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That would be helpful if you could do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand this as your permission, and I will try to make that telephone call and check. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours will understand, of course, that the Prosecution looks for, has looked for, and always seeks to find documentary support for such assertions, not always with the cooperation of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document is dated the 19th of July from the Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, unit for anti-terrorist operations. What do you know about that? Mr. Stevanovic, what do you know about the anti -- the unit for anti-terrorist operations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood that I should read the text first. First of all, I'm not familiar with the unit for anti-terrorist operations. I know about the special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Vasilije Mijovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vasilije Mijovic is somebody I know. For a while, he worked at the training camp for the training of special police units at Mount Tara, and Franko Simatovic found him at my request. Before that, Mr. Stojicic insisted through the state security sector that assistance be given me in finding instructors. I know this man as an instructor who was involved in the training of special police units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He writes --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "We hereby inform you that the ATD unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia was ordered to pull back from the zone of combat operations in the Trnovo sector by 1200 hours on the 20th of July ... in order to undertake other assignments." What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only conclude that this is related to the previous documents. But Vasilije Mijovic never belonged to the state security sector, and I don't know at which time he belonged to the state security sector, but he could not write or sign this document according to all I know. And anyway, I see that this document isn't signed at all, although this may be a teletype copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document, dated the 21st of July, signed from the Republika Srpska deputy minister or, rather, for the Deputy Minister Tomislav Kovac. And this refers to the Jahorina training camp of the Special Police Brigade which has informed the writer on the 18th and 19th of July this: "... during the execution of a combat task in the area of Bratunac-Srebrenica-Konjevic Polje, four members of a unit made up of conscripts brought from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia deserted. Their whereabouts are unknown. They left weapons and equipment in the room in which they were accommodated." And then it sets out their names: Dragan Okiljevic, Zelimir Glogovac, Slavko Djukaric, and Savo Filipovic. Two things: This is, of course, in the period of the Srebrenica massacre and killings, killings that took days to achieve. Do you know what combat task in the area of Bratunac-Srebrenica-Konjevic Polje might have led men from Serbia to desert?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot answer this question. I simply don't know. I am seeing this document from the first time. But I remembered something in relation to the previous document. That previous document could have been written by way of misrepresentation. That is my opinion. Vasilije Mijovic allegedly signing something on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, that is simply incredible. Now, speaking about this, I don't know this document again, and what I -- I also don't know the reason for these people's desertion. Reasons for that sort of thing may be different. Obviously, the subject here is the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the question asked by Mr. Nice, it was put the wrong way because these conscripts are not from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. It says clearly "Members of a unit made up of conscripts brought from the FRY," and they are therefore conscripts of the army of Republika Srpska, because you can see that out of these four, almost all are from Bosnia and Herzegovina. According to the personal information we see against their names, they are conscripts of the army of Republika Srpska. One was born in Sarajevo, another one in Knezevo, another one in a village near Bugojno. So they -- one was born in Miljevina. So they are conscripts from Republika Srpska, not from the FRY, all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you say Mr. Nice misstated the evidence. Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I did, unintentionally. Not sure that I did. The point of the question is to ask the witness whether he knows, and he tells us he doesn't, of an incident or of an event in the course of a combat task which could lead men to desert. I've had his answer on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask your permission to make one more comment. It is really a problem for me to provide a relevant answer on a document I don't know after only two seconds after the question. And second, after the statement made by the Prosecutor, I simply didn't have time to answer. I didn't have the opportunity to reply to some of the statements made by the Prosecutor. I would not like that to be treated as non-responsiveness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you will be allowed time to read the document, and you must satisfy yourself that you understand the document and the information in it before you answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- another document. This is a document dated the 21st of July, coming from Srbinje public security centre, signed by acting chief Rade Radovic, and it addresses Ministry of the Interior in Pale, gives an account of recent events on the Trnovo-Kalinovik front, and then says: "In these operations, Andrija Mitrovic, son of Cedomir, a member of Rudo SJB, and two members of the 11th HP were killed..." The following MUP members were injured: Then the first four: Ratko Mitrovic, Simo Gajic, Srdjan Marinkovic, Milovan Neskovic, and the ninth, Nogo Jankovic, are all described as Serbian MUP. Your comment, please.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is really what we read here, but I don't know any of these four or five persons and I don't believe they belong to the MUP of Serbia. But as I said previously, I think we can check that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally at this stage, there may be one or two more documents we'll look at later, this one of the 24th of July, three days after you had escorted DutchBat through Serbia.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
