utterances.text: I have the impression that when you say I escorted the Dutch Battalion through Serbia you mean that I did it of my own accord and against the will of the Dutch battalion. I would like to be believe that it isn't so, though. It's simply the way you put it, it seems to be placed in a negative context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document reads, to the RS Ministry of the Interior from the police forces staff at Trnovo as follows: "The night on the Trnovo Battlefield went by in peace. The Banja Luka special police unit ... relieved the Serbia MUP unit Skorpions. No problems occurred in the course of the rotation." Signed by, or printed signature, of Savo Cvijetinovic. It could hardly be clearer, Mr. Stevanovic, that a unit of the Serbian MUP by the name of Skorpions had been on the territory of the Trnovo battlefield area right through the period of the Srebrenica massacre. The documents make it crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is crystal clear from the documents is that a unit of the Serbian MUP called Skorpions was escorted out of that part of the battlefield, but I'm telling you again that this unit has nothing to do with the police units of the MUP of Serbia. Why this is written in such a way is something that we have to get an explanation on from the person who signed this. I don't know how to explain it. Maybe those units posed as being something they were not, but I can tell you that the Skorpions have nothing to do with the MUP of Serbia or any of its police units. At the time, I was in control of the police units that were engaged across the border, and I can tell you for certain that none of those units went any further than they were taken by the assignments I have already explained. I don't know how to explain this, but I believe it can be checked. You are trying to check it through me, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you were introduced as the person who knew everything about what the MUP did in Bosnia and Croatia and to cover all aspects of this case. That's why I'm putting these matters through you. This is the document which I succeeded in burying, for which I apologise to everyone concerned, that we've now managed to disinter.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me answer. I had not understood my role here as having to provide answers to all questions from all aspects. I understood that I should provide answers to questions I know about. However, most of what you have asked me so far are things I know nothing about. You spent the entire day yesterday dealing with 1991, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and today with 1998. I'm sorry for being so lengthy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we see a document, The Muslim Factor. It's under cover of the 30th of June of 1995, and it sets out here: "On the 30th of June, 1995, activities that began on the Trnovo front the previous day continued. The combat group consisting of 5th special police detachment and two platoons each from Kajman, Plavi and Skorpia detachments attacked the Lucevik feature." No explanation for that document?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My explanation is the same as about the previous five or six documents. It is obviously a set of documents relating to the same region, the same time, and obviously done at the same command. And as you can see, the Serbian MUP is always in brackets. If the Serbian MUP had been present there, that commander would probably have had a correspondence with his own ministry and we would have seen a document that is part of a correspondence between that unit and the ministry of Serbia. In these papers, obviously there is just a reference to a unit of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who Slobodan Medic is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no idea who Slobodan Medic is. Is that really your answer? Think a bit.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Medic. I know one Medic at the MUP of Serbia, but I don't know who Slobodan Medic is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm concerned with the man who ran the Skorpions. Do you not know him?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I met in Baranja several people from that unit when I was there in 1995, but I don't know who Slobodan Medic is. Let me be precise: That was in Erdut. But I don't know who Slobodan Medic is, and I don't know the names of those people I met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me explain to you what I suggest is a relevant part of the truth, and that is that a unit of Skorpions passed into the area of Srebrenica before the massacre and took part in the killings of the people from Srebrenica. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you were a necessary component of the passage of that group into Republika Srpska because they had to pass a border that was under --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps then you'd be good enough to help me with this: When I asked you -- I think you'll find the map helpful. When I asked you on the basis of information --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you on the basis of information available to the Prosecution about the crossing that that unit is said to have used, I said the following, and I'm going to read from the transcript. I said: "The border that you supervised and other troops supervised went down to Priboj," and you said, "Yes, up to Priboj or, rather, the border with Montenegro." I asked you, "Priboj is sort of to the east --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's an error here. Not to Prijedor but to Priboj. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Priboj, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- I said, "Priboj is sort of to the east of Gorazde, isn't it?" "I think so, at least," you said. And I said, "Just north of Priboj there's a little crossing called Raca." And you said, and now please look at the map. You said, "There is a Raca, but I'm not sure whether it's a crossing. I don't recall whether it is in fact an official crossing. There is an official border crossing at Uvac and Kotorman." And so if we look at the map we see that Uvac is exactly where Raca is, and you knew perfectly well what I was speaking about, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I absolutely did not know what you were talking about. Uvac is the official border crossing. I am aware that there is a Raca, but I was unable to identify it immediately. I trusted what you were saying. Later on, I recalled that there is an official border crossing called Raca, which is in the northern part of the border between Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbia. Uvac, however, is an official border crossing and it cannot be linked to Raca. Of course it can if you look at the map, but then that looks leading. I had no idea that Raca was actually close to the border crossing of Uvac. I also explained that it's absolutely illogical to cross the border here in order to go to Srebrenica. It's especially illogical if it's being done by a unit which is part of the MUP of Serbia. Please look at the map and look where Srebrenica is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you please listen to me. I have more questions to ask you.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... entitled to answer because it's an issue of cross-examination that has imposed the witness's credibility on the line, the witness wants to give a full explanation. The transcript was read out, the witness pointed out what he knew and he wishes to go on and qualify it and he should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue with the explanation and finish it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I began to say the following: Were your assumption correct that a group of Skorpions was under the control of the Serbian MUP and that it went to Srebrenica to do something, then the use of the Uvac border crossing, and even more so the alternative, so to speak, Raca border crossing to go to Srebrenica would have been completely illogical because there is an official border crossing in Bajina Basta, which is much closer to Srebrenica, as you can see. And there is another one at Ljubovija near Bratunac. So on the assumption that what you are saying is true, it would be illogical to send that unit to this border crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two points. First --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My microphone's on, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I said that the unit was going directly to Srebrenica, then that was an error by me and I'm not sure that I said it. You may have inferred it. Because if this unit was going, as it was, to Jahorina and to Trnovo, coming from Djeletovci in Croatia, it would be entirely sensible -- may I offer a guide because we don't have all the places on this single map. This unit was going from, as we can see at the top -- perhaps the -- from Djeletovci in Croatia, and if it was going to get down to south of Srebrenica, further down, and to Jahorina, Trnovo for the Treskavica front, it would be entirely sensible for it to go south through Serbia and then to turn west and enter the Republika Srpska through Raca. Do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Even with this explanation, the Raca crossing, as you call it, would not have been sensible. Even had the unit gone through Serbia from Srem, it would have been logical to go towards Kotorman and Visegrad because that's a much shorter route, and then go to Gorazde, Jahorina and so on via Visegrad. There is not a single reason for them to go on through Prijepolje and Priboj by a circuitous route in order to reach that destination. However, we are now dealing with hypotheses and assumptions, not facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, the second point I wanted to make from your answer, which I don't think you have answered, is this: When I asked you about Raca, before I had made that atlas available to you, as the transcript reveals, you showed that you knew immediately what I was talking about because you spoke of Uvac and you then subsequently tried to change your position. Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not the truth. Please, Mr. Prosecutor, that is not the truth. I was at the Uvac border crossing. I've been there hundreds of times, that is. I know that there is a geographical term Raca, but I had no idea it was in the immediate vicinity. You can be sure of that. And let me respond to something you have said. I completely reject any thought that I knew that some paramilitary units had crossed over from Serbia into Republika Srpska in order to perpetrate crimes. This cannot be brought into any kind of connection with myself as a professional. I would not have tolerated any such thing. I would not have turned a blind eye to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some extracts from a video. The video lasts about two hours but it will only be a few minutes of it that we will show in order to give its context. It comes in several clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While the clips are being played and with the -- the learned Judges might like a copy of this map, I think. It's only -- it doesn't have to become an exhibit. It's just a guide to the general territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we see here, we see here a ceremony of the Skorpions being blessed by a priest, and this is happening at Djeletovci. And so that you can understand the usefulness of the film, we may get to the point where they come individually to be blessed so that they have full facial views provided for us, many or most of them, if not all of them.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the faces very clearly. I don't know if it's the quality of the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as necessary, I will help you later with freeze-frame pictures to make life easier. To save time, we'll move to the next clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, you can see the date, 25th of June. This is the same unit on its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We saw there, of course, the sign of Pale, it having already entered Republika Srpska via, as I'm suggesting, Raca and now being on the -- to the east of Sarajevo at Pale. Next clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're now at Jahorina, as we can see from the map we've got. Some with red berets, as you can see. Next clip.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see this picture very clearly. If the image can be brought into better focus, that would be much better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... angle of the screen to make sure the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a very bad angle here. Can this be rectified?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry that you've had that inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can it be rectified? If it can, then let that be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is at -- this is at Trnovo at the command post of the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is on the front at Treskavica, or was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this -- pause there. This video, which is potentially distressing viewing and I'm only going to play very small parts of it, reveals, Mr. Stevanovic, if the evidence is in due course admitted, and that's why I want your assistance, reveals that men were brought from Srebrenica in batches to this group of Skorpions to be executed and they were executed, and what you see here is a lorry load of six young men. This is the same truck with the men in the back. And you can see the red berets.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, but I don't see or, rather, I haven't seen any Skorpio insignia so far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'd recognise the Skorpio insignia, would you, if you saw it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be clear. I don't know exactly what it looks like, but I assume that there's a picture of a scorpion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just guessed that, did you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, in Erdut I had occasion to see several members of this unit. I think they were in uniform and had insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we just pause for one minute, please. Your Honours, exceptionally I'm going to make a very rapid phone call, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Press on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The lorry leaves. The men are eventually taken up into the hills. It may be difficult to move it, but I don't need to linger on this. Here they are taken up into the surrounding countryside. Two remaining not shot are untied. I needn't go into the detail, or we needn't view the detail. They're untied, they move the four bodies, and then they are themselves shot, and I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've reduced for your assistance and for ours -- yes. And in answer to your observation about looking for Skorpio insignia, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, can you tell us about that film?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, to a degree I will. But if I can just deal with --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We haven't established any foundation for this. To my mind, this looks like sensationalism. There are no questions directed to the witness on the content of that film in a way that he can deal with it. It's merely been a presentation by the Prosecution of some sort of material they have in their possession that has not been disclosed to us and then it has been shown for the public viewing without any question attached to it. It's entire sensationalism. It's not cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, there is some merit in that. That's why I asked what are we going to be told about the film. Who made it, in what circumstances, and what questions are you putting to the witness in relation to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. I'm coming to that. As to the -- as to the film, my suggestion to the witness is that this is a film showing, as it happens, Skorpions executing prisoners from Srebrenica. And the questions I wanted to ask him and want to ask him are as follows: In light of his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let him answer that question first.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly, he can answer that question, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting this film shows Skorpions executing prisoners from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I am upset, I have to say that this is one of the most monstrous images I have ever seen on a screen. Of course I have never seen anything like this in -- live. I am astonished that you have played this video in connection with my testimony because you know full well that this has nothing to do with me or the units I commanded. I attempted to explain this yesterday, and I have also attempted to explain it today. I'm not saying that you do not have the right to do this, but I have to say that I am really upset --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you agree with the -- do you agree with the Prosecutor's suggestion or proposition that this is a film that shows Skorpions executing prisoners from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I do not intend to cast doubt on what the Prosecutor is saying, but I have not seen a single person I know here, and I have seen no evidence that this is the unit in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to -- in answer to your second point, did you not observe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll come back to two matters of detail later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want your assistance with the following. If these still pictures from the film, shown for the context for it to be understood, and I want your assistance now or later with my suggestion to you that that film, now available - and it's a film, Your Honour, taken clearly by members of the unit covering the period of time from the end of June until after Srebrenica - I want your assistance, please, now or later, with the identification of and with the function of the people we can identify from this film. The first one, the leader of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Slobodan Medic, and there are two photographs of him. Do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall only the nickname. The nickname Boca is familiar, but I cannot recall his face. I think I saw a man with this nickname in Erdut in 1995 on two or three occasions, but he did not come to see me. I saw him, if I recall rightly, at Mr. Milanovic's place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was the man who headed the Skorpions from the time when they guarded the oil fields in Djeletovci right through to his engagement of the Skorpions in Kosovo, because we're going to come to Kosovo as soon as we can. Is that the man?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I explained about Djeletovci, that I don't know, I don't know what he was doing. I saw him on two or three occasions, I told you where, but I had nothing to do with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not clear about that answer. Are you acknowledging, General, that that is Boca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not acknowledging that because I can't recall his face. All I recall is the nickname Boca in a group of five or six men whom I saw three times at the most, on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's a person you saw as a member of the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph, and again what's been done in order to assist you to help us is to take photographs that we assert are connected. This is Branislav Medic, also known as Cipa, seen killing the fourth person, I think, to be killed, but then seen face on. Are you able to recognise the man at all from that photograph or do you know the name?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not remember any other name or nickname. I just happened to recall the nickname of Boca, as I have already said, but I remember no other names or nicknames, nor was I ever told the first or last names. Perhaps they were introduced to me, yes, but I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go through the next pictures quickly. They're here for identification of the unit and for examination of to whom the unit was subordinated. The next picture is not shown at the killing site, is Nikola Kovacevic, also known as Nikica. In respect of all of these, I'm going to ask you, if you can, to help us with whether they were indeed members of a force subordinated to the MUP, but we'll go through them quickly because I don't expect you to say that you recognise one, but tell me if you do.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said more than once that they were not members of the MUP. This group and this formation or unit was not part of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Topic is the next one. The next one is Djuro Meleusic. The next one is Dragisa Zuber. The next one shown in four pictures is Pero Opacic, also known as Coke, and he is the man with the moustache, bottom right of the picture but also seen in other pictures, on the left the truck. Do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one, then, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you showed about three but didn't ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. I said that they were identified as people who were members of the unit, and I was going to ask him to identify if they were members of the unit now or in due course for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this one is Slobodan Davidovic, who was seen, it's going to be asserted, at the killing site. It's an older man. Do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I don't recognise any of the ones you've shown me so far. And otherwise, I knew nobody within that unit nor could I recognise them at all. I have nothing in common with them, nothing to do with them at all, and I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the next one. Petar Dimitrovic. You see him, both at the bottom and at the top. It's the man on the left this time at the bottom, in red berets. Do you recognise the uniform?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to patches -- you made an observation about patches. Let me ask you this question: Were you aware that units travelling from Serbia to Republika Srpska to fight there would change their patches, their identifying patches, as they moved from one country to the other? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Changing their patches? That is something that I don't know about, that they changed their patches when crossing the border. Possibly that is true, but I was not aware of it. Border crossings were not under my control in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next picture, please. Slobodan Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the next one, who it is said is one of those engaged in the killing, is Pero Petrasevic. He can be seen on the top right-hand picture on the right. He can be seen shaving, I think, on the top left. The next picture --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Few more to go through because I want your help. Milorad Momic, the next one, also to be seen at the killing site. A man who's only identified by the nickname Siptar, we can see is the man being blessed, on the left, by the priest and one of those engaged in the killing. Does the name Siptar or the man shown mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one is a person whose first name is unknown, but Grubor. And the next one, if you don't know him, and I don't imagine you will, is the -- the next one is Branislav, and he is the man standing with folded arms. For us, the man on the left of the two, standing with folded arms and with a visible moustache.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the first man or the other one. I've never seen them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then we come to Milko, whose last name is not known. So that I can complete the numbers, there's only about eight to go. The next one is -- first name not known. Next picture, please. Hovan. The next one is first name not known, Djurik. The next one is a person who was indeed a bus driver who was involved, the bus driver from Srebrenica called Braco. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next picture is a picture of Aleksandar Medic, who is one of those who engaged in killing. We can see him being blessed and in other pictures. Then we come to Sasa, similarly implicated in the killings themselves. Then we have Branislav Medic. This scene is not from a scene on the way to the killing site, it's a scene elsewhere in the video. The next one is Srdjan Manojlovic, who it's said is a VJ captain, or was. The next one is Srecko, last name unknown. The penultimate one is -- ante-penultimate one is first name unknown Miljkovic. The penultimate one is Olujic; and the last one is Branislav. We've provided you -- I have provided you, as a senior member of the police at the time and still engaged by the MUP, with the allegations that we are able to make about this event counter to what you have said about the good behaviour of Serb forces in Republika Srpska. Two things: How can you help us, please - because you said you would help - check on the function of these men in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But -- but please, allow me to answer the question first. I did not say anything about the conduct and behaviour of the Serb forces in Republika Srpska. You say something like that and then you go on to the question and I'm not given a chance to answer the previous question and then it turns out that I agree with you. I really don't remember having said anything about the good behaviour of Serb forces in Republika Srpska. All I said was this: I said that the police forces whom I led, whom I -- who I was in charge of with respect to Bajina Basta, Priboj, Rudo, and Visegrad, and in connection with the involvement of PJP units in the Banja Luka, Prijedor, and Doboj regions, with respect to those units I said what I said, and I repeat that those units were extremely professional and performed their police duties in the best professional way possible, and they cannot be linked in any way to any crimes whatsoever. Everything else that you have shown me has absolutely nothing to do with me. Of course I'm a witness and I will view what you're showing me and answer what you ask me, answer every question you ask me, but these are not questions that I should be asked because I have nothing to do with this group nor do my units have anything to do with this group whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow, then, for the possibility that a unit subordinated to the MUP of Serbia and calling itself the Skorpions was on the territory of Republika Srpska in the area of Jahorina and was involved in killing people from Srebrenica? Do you allow that possibility?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the public security sector, I do not allow the possibility, but as to the state security sector, I have no knowledge about that. I don't believe it either. I assume, I suppose, that I would have to know about something like that had something similar happened, even if it is the state security sector that is involved, although I did say in principle that that didn't come under my purview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You were -- you were distracted by the comment that preceded the previous question from actually answering the question. The question was: Is there some assistance you can give in trying to establish the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- whether these were personnel involved in a unit called the Skorpions in June 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't be of more assistance than I was, having said what I said. If you have a more concrete question which would be of assistance, I'm here and happy to help you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the question was asked because in relation to some of the earlier documents you made the comment that you could make inquiries. Now, is that not something that can be done in relation to the material that's now been presented to you in this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Along those lines, of course, I think I can. I don't know what the response will be from the organs involved, but if you give me a list of names at the end of my testimony, I could check it out and see whether they were members of the MUP or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, that's why I've provided you with the context and the setting of the film, taken quite shortly, and with these stills. Now, are you prepared to use your powers to try and confirm or otherwise that these men were indeed members of the Skorpions in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't, of course, check that out, whether somebody was a member of a group that I don't know existed or where it existed and under whose command it was. I know about the group from 1995, because quite simply, in a place there I saw three or four men who introduced themselves as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. being those men, and the name seems to ring a bell in my ears, but I really don't know what the group was about, under whose force it came, and where it was. I didn't deal with groups. I don't know where the Serb Volunteer Guard was, for example, or other similar groups. I don't know any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stevanovic, the reason I asked you, or I followed up on Mr. Nice's question was because you refute any connection between that activity on the video and the public security part or the public part of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you went on to say that you didn't believe it could be part even of the state security section of the MUP. And you also said in that answer that if it had been, you were bound to have known about it. And that's why I followed the question up to see if there were inquiries you could make to establish whether these persons were in some capacity engaged by the MUP in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said that I could try to establish the facts, I stem from the supposition that the ministry and sector in the ministry would provide me with that information if I made the request. In the ministry, they should have the overall information of all the employees in the ministry to the present day for given periods of time. The only problem that can exist is if the information system were destroyed by the bombing of the building itself. That's the only problem that could exist. The ministry in its archives does have a list of all its staff, and that would not be too great a problem, shouldn't be a great problem. The state security sector, in the personnel sense, was relatively separate, but once again, I do believe that documents and records about their staff exist too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If it would be convenient, I have just one -- two more questions or two more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On this issue, and just so I can make my position plain to the witness, and then I'll turn to another topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Stevanovic, I don't want you to be under any illusion, but I want your assistance if you'll give it. But my suggestion to you is this: That that group couldn't have got into Republika Srpska through Raca without the complicity and knowledge of those who had control of the crossings, and thus you must have known that this group was going in. Do you see? That's the suggestion I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. It is not the correct suggestion. I had no reason to know, nor was I in charge of who was crossing a border crossing either way. That is something that the sector of the border police was in charge, and I have said that several times. Apart from that, in addition to that, the stepped-up measures, or especially stepped-up measures, if I can put it that way, were applied from Bajina Basta south of the border with Montenegro and not to the north. Of course, there were stepped-up measures of some kind, but the stepped-up measures that we discussed in this courtroom, they should be linked and related just to Bajina Basta and southward towards the Montenegrin border, and that is clearly explained in my responses earlier on. Now, whether somebody at some point can cross a border unlawfully at other crossings, it is general common knowledge that they can. On the other hand, some members of the army of Republika Srpska and the army of Republika Srpska Krajina had their domicile and residence in Serbia and normally crossed the border. The regime of border crossings was such that ID cards were used. You needed identification cards and no other travel documents. So anybody could cross the border when they so wished with an ordinary ID card in regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, to the extent that your question operates on the basis that the witness had control of the border crossing, my understanding of the evidence, of his evidence, is that border crossing is a matter that falls within the control of a special unit in the Ministry of the Interior. He went there with his forces to assist. It is not his evidence that he had control of the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour's, I think, correct in an analysis of the spoken words of the evidence. My proposition, however, and it doesn't need further answer from the witness, would remain the same, the proposition being that if you have a person of this seniority there to engage in support of the kind he said, you couldn't do something of this nature without running the risk of displeasure from the authorised person if what was being done wasn't authorise. So it's as simple as that. May I put my other point just before the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second point I want to put to you is built on the questions I asked you about your being a trusted individual. That's why I asked you about that. And I'm going to suggest to you this: That by the 21st of July, well after a week from the first communications of which we've heard going to your government, you could only be trusted to get that near to Srebrenica and to take the DutchBat out if you were trusted to deal with the knowledge of the massacre, and that's the suggestion. So my question to you, with that background, is this: When you were sent by your deputy minister, assistant minister, were you told that there had been a serious massacre or serious event happening at Srebrenica? Were you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me say that your previous observations are completely incorrect. And secondly, let me say that none of that was told to me by anybody, absolutely not. Nor was I able to make any conclusions about that from what I saw in Bratunac and from the brief contact I had with the leadership of the DutchBat. So rest assured that I am telling you only the truth --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will provide the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I will provide the witness, if the Court is content with this, with the photographs and names for him to make such inquires as he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. On that note, we will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to turn to a much later event, Mr. Stevanovic, today; Dubrava. One of the reasons I'm turning to that is this is something of which you do have some personal knowledge, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have partially already explained that I have something to do with Dubrava in the sense that I was in charge of talking to the representative of the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Justice had a request whereby the MUP should be included into the evacuation of prisoners from Dubrava prison after the bombing of that prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, please? We know that you told us you were present when they -- when they left the prison, the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never present in the prison itself. I was in Pristina at the time of the bombing, or perhaps a day later. What I remember very well is when I think the assistant minister of justice arrived - his surname is the same as my own - and when just before his arrival the minister called me and told me that I should receive that colleague from the Ministry of Justice and to give him assistance concerning the evacuation of the prisoners from the KPZ Dubrava to the KPZ Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us on the last occasion you spoke of this that the head of staff of the headquarters, you thought on the 23rd of May, sent out an order ordering the SUP of Pec to give officials -- assistance to the officials of the prison; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no part of that you wish to change?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dubrava --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I was understood correctly, but what I said I stand by now too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dubrava has been somewhat thinly sketched as to its history by the Prosecution, and I want a little more assistance from you on that. It was built in the 1980s, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I did read about when it was built somewhere, but I don't remember. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was to be one of the very largest prisons in Europe. I think it was going to be the second or third largest prison in Europe. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. But I do know that it was a large prison. It covered a large area, surface area. There were a lot of facilities and buildings. I flew over the prison in a helicopter and I think I only went inside once, but I'm not quite sure whether I did in fact or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For any who have not been there, you've flown over it. First of all, we can see Istok up there. It's in a remote corner of territory, and it is itself set in very wide landscape. Do you remember that? You can see Istok but I don't think the prison is itself marked. Remote landscape, yes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was relatively unpopulated, the area, but it was more populated than you could tell by looking at this map, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed when it was built, as the material already before the Judges reveals, although we haven't focused on it yet, some thought that it was built for purposes additional to the holding of prisoners. Is it right that people thought it was to serve a purpose additional to the holding of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. What other purpose it had or for what purpose it had been planned for, in that sense I answered that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice and the witness, I apologise. We need to stop for a minute for technical reasons relating to the operation of the Albanian booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I will stay standing, if you don't mind. My chair is occupied with files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1999, you were -- you had your ministerial position, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not getting any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving the interpretation, I apologise. It seems that when we had that technical adjustment, all the channels were switched off, so somebody would have to adjust the witness's channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we are on now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1999 you occupied your ministerial position.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was assistant minister but not the minister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that give you oversight of all aspects of the MUP's work?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all levels and not in all aspects. I was the assistant of the minister. I attended the collegium of ministers, and all the questions that were discussed at that level in principle I was acquainted with, of course, when I attended those meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we saw from the documents we looked at yesterday for the earlier period, 1998, that you were a regular attender at the Joint Command on the ground in Kosovo. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "regular." At meetings which those individuals attended, I, too, attended perhaps some ten times, give or take five, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here's something I suggest you must have --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I didn't attend regularly. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here's something that I suggest you must have known about, although we have yet to hear about it, and it's what happened to the prison in about June of 1998. Think back, please, and think what it was that happened to the prison in about June of 1998.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened in the prison?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Please remind me and I'll certainly tell you if I know about it. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was depopulated of prisoners and taken over by the JSO under Legija and Simatovic. Now, think back. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no need for me to think it over. I have knowledge about that. I thought you meant what happened in the prison. In my mind it associated me with an event in the prison which would be security related. Now, in the course of 1998, indeed, in part of the prison was the headquarters of the JSO, the unit for special operations. I know about that but I don't know that the prison was depopulated of prisoners because of that. Possibly they were, but I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this may, of course, be the backdrop to the NATO bombing, but we'll come to that later. In 1998 this was a place from which Simatovic's units under Legija, with Stanisic's oversight, was operating in the general area of Kosovo to which Istok is close; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a part or, rather, KPZ Dubrava was indeed used as a headquarters for that special unit, the JSO, and of course while it was residing there, it was from those headquarters that it was sent out on assignment in conformity with the plans in which that unit took part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who directed that unit in its operations against the KLA from Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit, as is well known, was within the composition of the state security sector. It came under that. Now, in the main operations that we discussed at previous meetings, that unit was included in keeping with a plan which was a general plan and related to the entire region of Kosovo and Metohija, and in keeping with individual orders which we have had occasion to see. Of course, they did not take part in all the actions, all the operations, just some of them in keeping with the individual orders issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the JSO unit leave the prison in 1998?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the degree to which prisoners repopulated or, alternatively, increased the population of the prison? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Into 1999, forces were located close to the prison. They weren't now in the prison, but there were forces located close to the prison, both the JSO and also other forces. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know the exact positions of the forces during 1999, so I can't remember. Quite possibly they were, however, I cannot confirm the exactitude of that fact. The units were in the entire region. I have explained that no unit used its peacetime location because of the danger and threat of the bombing. So all the units used a number of reserve locations from which they were able to do the job entrusted to them. Possibly one of these units were near Dubrava, but I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A reserve force unit from Krusevac, for example, being close to the prison? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't remember, but if you could assist me; is it a police or a military unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's a military unit.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something I cannot know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which brings us then to your analysis of and evidence about the bombing of Dubrava prison. Your sources of information are documents? Yes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Documents and some telephone and verbal information I received while I was in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- the verbal information came from who?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the secretariat in Pec. I don't know the man personally. Plus I had information that came into the staff itself from the secretariat in Pec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any of the people who provided you with information at this stage?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might make a mistake. I can name the people who would be the logical source of such information. The chief of SUP at that time was Boro Vlahovic. The chief of the police section was a man whom I know but I can't recall his name at the moment. Deputy chief of SUP was a Mr. Vulevic. Or maybe I could have gotten information from the shift leader. The important thing was to get information. Who you get it from was less important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you were asked questions by the accused and he took you to Exhibit 204, you read the paragraph and you said, "NATO bombing was repeated from 1700 hours to 1805 hours and then again at 23 hours, and on the 22nd of May, 1999, at 0610 hours." Are you able from your own knowledge to say anything about any of those alleged times of bombing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot help you with the times. When I read the documents, I identified the 19th, 21st, 22nd, 24th. That's true if that's what it says in the transcript, but I don't know the exact hours. I believe the bombing was repeated on three occasions. I believed an on-site investigation was resumed three times and that the evacuation of the prisoners took place on the 24th or maybe the 25th. That's the recollection that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let's just go back for one second to the takeover of the prison or, as you would say, part of the prison, in 1998 by the JSO. That needed approval at what level?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of the two ministries. The prison certainly could not have been used without the approval of the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's go back to the timing of the bombs. If I suggest to you that 6.10 in the morning is a calculated fabrication by those who have recorded that time, what do you say?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the claim that it is a fabrication is inaccurate. Of course, I don't know which document we are talking about. I can't remember at this moment. But I would not accept that any fabrication is contained in the documents in these files.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a policeman you would accept, would you not, that it's a very useful exercise to look at what someone, a defendant or a body charged with impropriety, to look at what that individual or body says or records over a period of time. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll move on. We'll look at the first document. Tab 202 is where we go first. So this is a defendant's tab, tab 202. And what we notice from this document is nothing more, really, than that under "Dubrava" -- you'll need the -- for the 21st of May, on the first page, it records that the -- between 8.30 and 2345 hours on the 21st of May there was attack, 47 high-explosive missiles, and it asserts that 93 prisoners were killed. Now, whose is this document? Can you tell us? It's not signed. Whose --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already explained this. This is a summary of the entire case file on Dubrava, drawn up at the Ministry of the Interior, because it was received as such by Defence advisors -- counsel, by Defence counsel. But there should be accompanying material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is nothing to identify this document, if we look at the original, of any kind. It only covers the days 19th and 21st, so it doesn't deal with the 22nd at all, but it does suggest that 93 prisoners died. Now --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in this document, in the second line -- the second paragraph, rather, sub-heading "21st of May."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've had evidence from three live survivors of Dubrava, and as to that day, the night of the 21st, they say that either - and they give three different figures - one says 18 to 19, one says 19, and one says 23 prisoners, but nothing at all like 93 prisoners. You can't vouch for the accuracy of this document at all, can you? It's anonymous. We don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have explained, but I can say it again. I am sure that this document was supplied from the official documentation of the Ministry of the Interior. Prima facie we cannot see any marking or identification, but it is a summary of the remaining documents which are attached, and everything that is written here should be supported and proven by the documents that follow and that can be identified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall exactly now, but I seem to recall that this is an excerpt from a document that was tendered as an exhibit during the testimony of the chief of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs, Mr. Paponjak, as part of a broader document that lists all incidents involving loss of life that happened on the territory of the SUP of Pec, and this one relates only to Dubrava. But I don't have the Paponjak documents here with me. And we'll be able to check that anyway. I believe this is an excerpt from that document, and that document was drawn up by the Ministry of the Interior covering all secretariats. The one in question here is the secretariat in Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your point being then that the document should be looked at as a whole. You produced it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, let me make my position clear. I'm suggesting to the accused through the witness, or to the witness, I don't know who it is, that the total of 93 prisoners is a false and indeed an intentionally false figure, for reasons that will emerge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand me, Mr. Stevanovic? I'm saying that the figure of 93 is inflated and intentionally so.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what you are saying. It's just that I cannot accept that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall we go next, then, please, to tab in your papers 208. This is a document which we didn't have, I think, in translation before. We do have in translation now. We've had it translated because it was a document of significance, and the process didn't seem to be bringing it to us in time. While that's coming around, the Chamber might like to look, and the witness might like to look at the last two sheets of the document, both at the change in the size of type, in the absence of a number from the top of the page, in any event as it's copied, and then we'll see the translation so far as it's relevant. Following in the original, please, Mr. Stevanovic, this document dated the 2nd of June, to your Minister Stojiljkovic, and delivered to others as well, including Milutinovic, we go over to the next -- second of the pages of translation, at the foot we see this: "NATO aggressor repeatedly attacked in the period between 8.20 and 10.30 on the 21st of May. During the attack, more than 25 projectiles of huge power were fired, almost completely destroying all the buildings." And then three lines on from that: "In addition, many convicts were killed in this strike. So far, 97 convicts were pulled out of the rubble," and then injuries are given. The next paragraph reads as follows, second line: "This was probably -- the surrounding wall was damaged. This was probably one of the aggressor's goals, taking into account that among the convicts there were some notorious terrorists and criminals who had killed several policemen and soldiers and for whom the International Committee of the Red Cross and other so-called humanitarian organisations showed interest for. Immediately after the surrounding wall of the institution had been damaged, a group of convicts attempted escape, but were prevented by a swift and efficient intervention of members of the Security Service, who, standing in circles around the institution walls, were maintaining security at a level determined by condition of permanent attacks and bomb raids." Can you tell me what that means, that last sentence?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This long sentence, "Immediately after the destruction of the surrounding wall, the perimeter wall..." is that the sentence you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last sentence I read, last sentence of the paragraph, where it says, "They were standing around maintaining security at a level determined by condition of permanent attacks ..."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what more I can tell you in addition to what you've read. The security detail secured the prison according to the established disposition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, there is no suggestion in the papers, nor, I take it, any information coming to you by word of mouth, that prisoners trying to escape were shot dead. Because if that had happened, it would have been properly recorded, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that I don't remember receiving such information that any escape attempts took place. We see some sort of reference to attempted escape here and an attempt to prevent it, but I personally did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not information to that effect, and I can interpret this document now just as competently as you or anybody else, but I think this sentence is self-explanatory. So there is an escape attempt. That's what it says here. I, of course, didn't have to know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me pause you there for a minute. We'll take our eyes off the document and just focus on the events. What happened was that after the bombing on the 21st, the prison was taken over in the early hours of the 22nd by special forces, and the prison guards were kicked out and the forces that came in were free to do what they wanted with the prisoners. That's what actually happened, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your claim. I don't agree with it, and I have no knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed I'm going to ask you this, since you were at a high level, accessible to ministers and trusted by them: Was there a plan to respond maybe to this bombing generally or particularly by killing all the Albanian prisoners in that prison? Was there a plan forged to do just that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not true. There was no such plan to kill anybody outside of situations prescribed by the law, and the law does not envisage any possibility to kill anyone deliberately. I said several times that death could occur only as an undesirable result of a lawful use of means of coercion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we know is that if any forces other than the prison service were to take over the prison, it would require a high-level decision, just as it had done in 1998. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That logic in itself is not good. If an event occurs involving loss of life, local police does not need any decision from higher up to take the prescribed lawful measures. It is quite a different case when a facility is taken over in order to be used for purposes other than peacetime purposes, so it can't -- what you said in your last statement cannot apply here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you understand by minister of interior special -- "Ministry of the Interior special units"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That concept has been misused very frequently. At the Ministry of the Interior, there is only one special unit. It is called the special anti-terrorist unit. I've explained several times that special police unit cannot receive --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... were doing. You would know what those units were doing in Kosovo in May of 1999.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean special purpose units and the special unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the units you've described. You would know what they're doing, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I knew in principle on what assignments they are there and on what assignments they're engaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the document, now, and you go down a couple of paragraphs, where it says: "NATO Air Force --" this is the top of our pages 4 or 5, where it says, "NATO Air Force is to date bombing Istok penal-correctional institution on a daily basis." Have you found that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document that we've got, dated the 2nd of June, simply isn't true, as a matter of fact and history, that NATO was bombing on a daily basis Istok penal-correctional institution. That's not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to put it this way would simply not be correct according to the information I have. I don't think it was the intention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next paragraph begins: "It has to be stressed," about its being an up-to-date institution and taking ten years to build, and then says this point that I referred you to earlier: "It accommodates 3.000 persons. According to some information, it was built for other purposes and its size could meet the needs of neighbouring countries." The other purposes were the security purposes reflected by Frenki and Legija coming with their unit there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know anything about this purpose. What could it possibly mean "to meet the needs of the neighbouring countries"? I don't know what would have attracted those units. All units were in search of appropriate locations, because there were many units who could not find an alternative location to their peacetime one. And all units needed to be put up in facilities that were the most appropriate to the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to go on two paragraphs, and we'll read this paragraph in full: "Ministry of the Interior -- Ministry of the Interior Special Units arrived to the institution at 0500 hours on the 22nd of May and entered the closed part while the guards of the institution withdrew, following the order of the Ministry of Interior representative, from the central part of the institution and positioned along the wider ring around the wall in order to prevent possible attempts of convicts to escape." I read on from the 5.00 reference to the next one. "Special units came at approximately 17.00 hours that same day, and at approximately 05.00 on the 23rd of March, 1999." 23rd of May, thank you, 1999. First of all, do you notice, Mr. Stevanovic, not a reference to the bombing at 6.10 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in this paragraph, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what we do notice is that if this paragraph is right, the prison is no longer populated by prison guards but is now populated by Ministry of Interior special units.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I believe this formulation is wrong. It's wrong to say special units. At the time, most policemen wore camouflage uniforms, either olive-grey or grey-blue, and every policeman wearing that uniform could perhaps be wrongly called special policemen. As to whether the prison guards left the prison, we can read that much, but it doesn't mean that they abandoned control over the prison. Rather, there was a redistribution of assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, really? Are you making it up as you're going along, Mr. Stevanovic, because you realise that this document should never have been included --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- aren't you? This document, I suggest to you - and it's a defendant's document - gives the game away. Let's just go back and let me help you with something. We had these three Prosecution witnesses who gave evidence, I can't remember how many years ago, but well before this document ever surfaced. They said this; that on the 21st, 23 prisoners were killed. On the 22nd of May, they were kept in the prison overnight and at 5.30 were lined up and then they were attacked from the -- they were lined up in the sports field and they were shot at and many of them were killed, 97 or thereabouts, from the watchtower. That's the account of one prisoner. 5.30 in the morning. The next prisoner, or the next witness, who was also a prisoner, gives an account of being ordered by guards to line up on the 22nd. The third witness, a similar account, but the first one actually gives the time; about half past five. Now, look at your document or, rather, the accused's document. "From 5.00 in the morning, pursuant to an order of the Ministry of the Interior, the prisoners of Dubrava were at the mercy of MUP special units staff." Will you tell me what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, of course, can only read what it says here. I can also say that it is normal that the police, after an event of that kind, goes on site to secure the area and to enable the investigating authorities to conduct their on-site investigation. I really can't see what they did here. I can only assume that they did what I said a moment ago. Of course, this should now be compared with the terms of on-site investigation as used and the other terms, and it is difficult for me on the basis of this documentation to go through the documents for purposes of a serious analysis. I am focusing my attention on this. Here we can indeed see that the units of the Ministry of the Interior had entered the internal -- or the institute's compound and that they went at 5.00 on the 22nd and at some other time, but I cannot say what they did there. I knew -- I know what is usually done after such an event, and I'm certain that that must be the content of the work of such units. We cannot see when the on-site investigation was conducted and the other details, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me assure you I'm going to give you a chance to go through the documents.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is quite clear. The decision made at the ministerial level -- help us with this: Would that be a decision that this accused would also have to approve in the setting of the problems in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What decision are you referring to? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The decision to put the MUP special units in at 5.00 on the morning of the 22nd. Would that be a ministerial decision, on your understanding, that this accused would have to approve?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such decision doesn't have to be taken at the level of the ministry or minister. If any facility of any area was bombed, and in that area there is at least one, even one wounded individual or even if the wounded did not exist, it is up to the Ministry of the Interior to go on spot, to secure the site, to take control of the site, to inform the judiciary and to assist them in conducting the investigation. For something like that, you don't need anybody's decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on two, pages, please, and you'll find at the foot of the page sentences that read like this: "On the 25th of May of 1999 in Pristina, authorised employees of the Ministry of Justice held a meeting with all --" then it breaks, and then over on the next page in type certainly of a different font size - I'm unable to say whether it's from the same machine - a non sequitur: "There were 1.079 prisoners in Dubrava penal-correctional institution. 96 were killed, three succumbed," and so on. Can you help me, please, with where I can find the proper following page to what we see at the end of your page 5? Where can I find the proper complete version of this document? Because this isn't it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, the following page is missing, at least. The text in big letters seems to be an attachment to something, not the continuation of this particular text. So in my tab, I really don't seem to have the last page, and quite obviously at least one more page should be in existence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Nice, may I ask this: Mr. Stevanovic, the units which are referred to as arriving at the institution at 5.00, that's 5.00 in the morning on the 22nd of May, these are units for which you would have -- or over which you would have control? They fall within your sector of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I did not have operative control over any unit in the Ministry of the Interior, and I explained that I was the assistant minister and that I went to Kosovo pursuant to his orders to perform concrete assignments with respect to his orders and requests and that I would report back to him from time to time. And I explained what the manner of control and leadership in Kosovo was like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question was not as clear as it should have been. You've been careful to distinguish in your evidence between the public sector and the security sector, the two elements in the MUP. Can I take it that this -- these units fell within the public sector for which you or about which you can speak with some authority? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that they do come under that, but I think that the wrong name was used, special MUP units, "Specijalne," because I don't believe that any special unit was there. I think that it was a local police unit that had authority in that particular sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you do appreciate that throughout your evidence in relation to these documents which come from the ministry you've been very anxious to talk them up, to tell us how authoritative they are, and this is the first example of one where you want to question its authority. Is that an accurate reflection of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't believe you followed that. I still consider these to be official documents of the Ministry of the Interior, so I stand by them as official documents of the Ministry of the Interior. I just tried to explain. This is a document of the Ministry of Justice. Quite possibly the person who compiled it didn't formulate the name of the unit in the proper way. Otherwise, I'm not challenging that this is indeed a document of the Ministry of Justice which is part of the documentation found in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also asked the question when we were looking at these exhibits. I asked Professor Rakic. I said that there needed to be one more page. There was a page missing. But as you can see, it says A/III. It is the document of the Ministry of Justice which the Ministry of the Interior disposes of, and my associates received it from the Ministry of the Interior. I didn't have time nor did my associates have time to look for the original document from the Ministry of Justice, but I do believe that we would be able to find it in the Ministry of Justice and that you can find the missing page. This whole set of documents was received from the Ministry of the Interior, however, and it has the A/III designation there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'd be grateful if I can complete what I was trying to do here. The reference A/III, that's a reference, do you say, that relates to the Ministry of justice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand that. What do you mean reference A/III?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you look at the front page of the document, on the top left-hand corner. You see the reference A/III, III.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is the reference of the Ministry of the Interior, but it was placed -- let me repeat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you said earlier --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you said earlier that these were references used by the Ministry of the Interior.
