utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So this is a document of the Ministry of the Interior or is it a document of the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is obviously a document of the Ministry of Justice which was included into the file of the Ministry of the Interior, and this reference was placed there subsequently on the title page, and also the other pages, as we can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll take the opportunity to deal with one more document, but we can see, just look at this, the cover page. The cover page is marked "Read this," it's signed by the minister, it's sent to Milutinovic, Marjanovic, Markovic, Stojiljkovic. It's a pretty serious document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously it is a serious document, and as the title says it represents an informational report on the attack on the prison at Istok, and it contains some other elements as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last page is not only in a different font size, but if you look at the top of the page, it doesn't have a page number. On your account it should be at least page 7, but it doesn't actually have a page number. Has this document been retyped, do you think?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has different attachment number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. May I just put one more document to this witness, with Your Honours' leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, one more before we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously this last page is not a component part of the previous document. It is a separate case, and you could see that if you look at the 010 attachment. So the case is the same but it is a different attachment, supplement. And the pages have been placed so as to suggest that it is one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That might be what makes it look suspicious, bearing in mind that there's no earlier reference to the victims of the bombing. That's the point that was long since made in the course of this examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I just want you to look at the next document, bearing in mind my suggestion to you that there was a planned massacre by the incoming special forces under your ministry to be put into effect on the morning of the 22nd and thereafter. This document before you comes from Aleksandar Rakocevic, the warden. We've seen another document from this man --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you have a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy a moment ago perhaps forgot to see. He says in the Ministry of Justice document there is no reference to the casualties, the victims of the bombing, as far as I understood it. Now, I'd like to draw his attention to the fact that on page 2 of the B/C/S or, rather, the Serbian text, it says quite clearly, "In this attack more -- a number of prisoners were killed" and in brackets, "(up to now 97 corpses were pulled out and 196 were wounded either more seriously or less seriously)." That's what the Ministry of Justice document says on page 2. And in that same paragraph in which it says that the deputy warden was killed, and so on and so forth. But Mr. Nice didn't quote that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we'll have to stop here. It's in the middle of the question, but -- no. We'll have to stop because we are going to trespass on the time of the following Court and then we'll be rebuked, as has happened before. We will adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of June, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
